title: Robotic Knee Replacement: What to Expect and Recovery Timeline
metaDescription: How robotic-assisted knee replacement works, who it suits, and a realistic week-by-week recovery timeline, from an orthopaedic surgeon in Thane West.
intro: Robotic-assisted knee replacement uses a 3D plan of your knee and a robotic arm that helps the surgeon keep each bone cut to that plan. Trials show it improves alignment accuracy; the long-term benefit over conventional surgery is not yet proven, and recovery still depends mostly on your health and rehabilitation.

sections.heading: How robotic surgery is different
sections.body: A CT-based or imageless 3D plan of your knee is created before surgery. During the operation, the robotic arm keeps bone cuts on plan and stops the saw outside the planned boundary, which is intended to protect healthy bone and ligaments. A 2024 review of nine randomised trials found more accurate alignment and slightly better patient-reported scores with robotic assistance, with longer operating time.

sections.heading: Typical recovery timeline
bullets: Day 0–1: Walking with support, often within hours of surgery
Week 1–2: Staircase training, daily physiotherapy, most patients home by day 2–3
Week 3–6: Walking unaided indoors, returning to desk work
Month 3: Most people are much more comfortable; some ache and swelling is still common, and continued strengthening matters
Month 6–12: Full benefit realised, including travel and recreational activity

sections.heading: Who is a candidate?
sections.body: Patients with advanced arthritis whose pain persists despite medication, physiotherapy and injections. Age alone is not a barrier — fitness for anaesthesia and motivation for rehabilitation matter more.

faqs.q: Is robotic knee replacement safer than conventional surgery?
faqs.a: The robot does not operate by itself; it helps the surgeon carry out the plan precisely. Randomised trials show more accurate alignment and small differences in early patient-reported scores, but no proven long-term advantage yet. Surgeon experience matters most.

faqs.q: How long does a robotic knee implant last?
faqs.a: There are no long-term data specific to robotic surgery yet. For knee replacements in general, registry analyses found about 93% still in place at 15 years and about 82% at 25 years.

faqs.q: When can I climb stairs after knee replacement?
faqs.a: Most patients climb stairs with support within the first week, and independently by 3–6 weeks, depending on muscle strength and physiotherapy compliance.
